findings.summary: The duplicated OKLab primitives in palette/core/oklab.ts have no working pin, and the durable fix is a collapse rather than a better test — but which shape to take is a design call.
findings.rationale:
CLAIM. srgbToLinear01 / linear01ToSrgb / rgbToOklab / oklabToRgb are hand copies of module-private functions in utils/colorUtils.ts. The stop-fitter measures error against GMT's real gradient pipeline, so if the two ever disagree the fitter optimises against maths the renderer does not use, and every fitted gradient is subtly wrong in a way no harness reports.

EVIDENCE. Measured 2026-07-29: perturbing rgbToOklab's first M-matrix coefficient by +0.0001 (0.024%) leaves the entire npm run test:palette chain green, exit 0, 44 passed 0 failed. +0.01 goes red but only at test-palette-generator.mts's tolerance round-trip ('reproduces slot A within 2 levels', got 4.43) — a tolerance small drift slips under. The assertion explicitly labelled 'oklab drift pin' reports 0 mismatches in both cases because it compares palette's re-exported lerpOklab against colorUtils' own, i.e. a function against itself.

OPTIONS.
(a) COLLAPSE — export srgbToLinear01 / linear01ToSrgb / rgbToOklab / oklabToRgb from utils/colorUtils.ts and re-export them from palette/core/oklab.ts, exactly the change already applied to gmtGradient.ts in P0a. Drift becomes structurally impossible instead of undetected, and the dead pin can then be deleted honestly rather than left as a marker. Widens colorUtils' public surface by four pure functions.
(b) REAL PIN — keep the duplication and rewrite section [4] to compare colorUtils.lerpOklab against a lerp composed from palette's own rgbToOklab/oklabToRgb. Requires reimplementing the polar (LCh) interpolation inside the guard; if the reimplementation is not faithful the pin fails for the wrong reason, and if it is faithful it is a third copy of the maths.
(c) TIGHTEN THE TOLERANCE on test-palette-generator.mts's round-trip so small drift is caught incidentally. Cheapest, but it makes an unrelated guard load-bearing for a contract it does not name, and it will go red for legitimate pipeline changes.
(d) Leave it; the risk is only realised if someone edits one copy.

RECOMMENDATION: (a). It is the change this codebase already chose once for the same problem, it removes the failure mode rather than detecting it, and it is the only option that lets the dead assertion be removed without losing coverage. Not applied here because it edits utils/colorUtils.ts, which is engine-core and outside this slice, and because deciding what belongs in colorUtils' public API is an architecture call.

The gap is documented in place either way — see the @assumption in palette/core/oklab.ts's header and the comment on section [4] of debug/test-palette-stopops.mts (commit 1e7802cf).

findings.summary: Eight of the 35 files in palette/core/ cannot be reached by any link in the test:palette chain, and the most consequential of them is gradientSeam.ts — the doc's own 'single conversion point' to GMT.
findings.rationale:
CLAIM. A transitive import walk from all 16 test:palette harnesses reaches 27 of the 35 .ts files under palette/core/. Unreachable: gradientSeam.ts, catalogLoader.ts, presetCatalog.ts, favientsExport.ts, favientDnd.ts, favientTargets.ts, rampCanvas.ts, storage.ts.

EVIDENCE. Reachability was computed by resolving every relative `from '...'` specifier from each harness (script kept out of the repo). Reachability is also an upper bound, not coverage: indesignIdml.ts and indesignIdmlTemplate.ts are reachable only because exportFormats.ts imports them, and the importformats harness never calls buildIdmlSwatchLibrary; img2grad/decode.ts is reachable but is the DOM decoder and is never invoked under node. Of the 16 export formats, only 6 (map, gpl, ggr, cpt, json, css) are exercised, by round-trip.

WHY gradientSeam.ts MATTERS MOST. palette-suite.md calls it the single conversion point from a 256-step ramp to a GMT GradientConfig and says 'Don't add a second ramp->stops path'. entryToGradientConfig / applyGradientConfig / applyEnvGradient encode real contracts — presets pass through as colorSpace 'linear' because that is what the fractal shader expects, applyEnvGradient forces 'srgb' because sky colour is displayed not radiance, SEAM_MAX_STOPS caps at 128 — and nothing checks any of them. A swapped colour space here miscolours every applied gradient and would not show up in any guard.

OPTIONS. (a) Add a debug/test-palette-gradientseam.mts pinning the colour-space contracts and the SEAM_MAX_STOPS cap against a stubbed store, and append it to the test:palette chain. (b) Extend the importformats harness to build and re-parse the remaining text formats, closing the exporter half. (c) Accept the gap for the DOM-bound files (rampCanvas, favientsExport, favientDnd, catalogLoader) which need a browser smoke, and cover only the pure ones. (d) Leave it.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) then (b). Both are new guard code, which is why neither was written unattended — a new harness that passes on first run has not been falsified, and falsifying it properly needs a quiet tree.

findings.summary: A .ugr collection export reduces to 64 RDP nodes but is silently exempt from the lossy-quality warning that .ai and .idml get.
findings.rationale:
CLAIM. collectionQualityWarnings() gates on `if (fmtKey !== 'ai' && fmtKey !== 'idml') return []`, so exporting favourites as .ugr never warns — even though exportFormats.ts reduces it through the same reduceStopIndices at UGR_MAX_STOPS 64.

EVIDENCE. EXPORT_FORMATS.filter(f => f.collection) evaluates to [ai, idml, ugr]. reduceStopIndices is called at line 345 with UGR_MAX_STOPS. aiLossyGradients measures reconstruction error at the 40-stop AI budget, so reusing it verbatim for .ugr would over-report; that is presumably why .ugr was excluded rather than an oversight, but nothing records the reasoning and nothing measures whether 64 nodes is actually safe.

OPTIONS. (a) Thread the per-format budget into aiLossyGradients and warn for .ugr at its own budget — correct, and turns a guess into a measurement. (b) Measure once offline whether 64 RDP nodes stays under AI_LOSSY_DELTA for the catalog, and if so keep the exemption but say so with a number. (c) Leave it — .ugr consumers are fractal tools that resample anyway, and Ultra Fractal's editor arguably prefers few draggable nodes to fidelity.

RECOMMENDATION: (b) first — it is a measurement, not a change, and it either justifies the current behaviour or turns this into (a). This is an export-fidelity product call, which is why it was not applied. The behaviour is now documented at the call site as an @assumption (commit 2576fab1).

findings.summary: The main img2grad harness stays fully green when a real crash bug is reintroduced into resample.ts; only the dedicated overshoot sweep catches it.
findings.rationale:
CLAIM. Removing the `if (i > n - 2) i = n - 2;` clamp from palette/core/img2grad/resample.ts reintroduces exactly the bug that clamp exists to fix. debug/test-palette-img2grad-overshoot.mts goes red immediately with the original error ('THREW: ... Cannot read properties of undefined (reading L)'). debug/test-palette-img2grad.mts — the main harness, 20 assertions — stays at '✓ ALL PASS', exit 0.

WHY IT MATTERS. The two harnesses sit next to each other in the chain and are named as though the second is a subset of the first. Anyone consolidating them, or dropping the '-overshoot' link as redundant, silently reopens a crash that reaches the user as a TypeError in the stop fitter. The overshoot sweep is 44 checks x 4 images x 11 colour counts x ~200 golden-hour steps x 3 spacings; the main harness uses a handful of fixed parameter sets, which is why it never lands on the overshooting combination.

OPTIONS. (a) Add a one-line note to both harness headers saying the overshoot sweep is not redundant and which regression it pins. (b) Fold a few overshooting parameter combinations into the main harness so it fails too. (c) Leave it.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), and it is nearly free. Not applied because both files are shared debug infrastructure and two other auditors were committing into this tree; a header edit there is better batched with the guard sweep.

findings.summary: npm run test:palette's twelfth link, test-engine-dnd-kernels.mts, imports nothing from palette/ at all.
findings.rationale:
CLAIM. Its only imports are ../store/dragFlight and ../store/sendTargetRegistry. It is an engine drag-and-drop kernel test living inside the palette chain, presumably because palette/core/favientDnd.ts is the main consumer — but favientDnd.ts is itself one of the eight core files no link reaches, so the association is conceptual rather than actual.

WHY IT MATTERS. Citing 'npm run test:palette' as the guard for a palette change is already coarse (16 links, most irrelevant to any one change); a link that touches no palette file at all makes it coarser and mildly misleading in commit messages. It also inflates the apparent coverage of the palette suite.

OPTIONS. (a) Leave it and name the specific link in guard citations instead of the chain — which the proposed palette rule below already does. (b) Move it to a test:engine-dnd script and cite that from a store-scoped rule. (c) Leave it and note the association in the chain.

RECOMMENDATION: (a). Splitting the chain is churn; the real fix is citing links, not chains. Worth pairing with the known check:rule-guards limitation that a chained npm script resolves by its FIRST command only, so a rule citing test:palette only ever resolves debug/test-palette-stopfit.mts.

INCIDENT — one commit is mis-attributed, and it was NOT a broad stage. Commit a2f1ec49 ('audit(p01a-palette-core): importFormats @invariant...') also contains 13 lines of palette/components/ChannelGraphEditor.tsx, which belongs to the p01b auditor. I staged one explicit path and checked git status --porcelain immediately before committing — ChannelGraphEditor.tsx was UNSTAGED at that moment. The p01b auditor staged it in the window between my status check and my commit, and `git commit` commits the whole index. No content was lost and history was not rewritten. The fix, used for every commit after that one: `git commit -F <msg> -- <paths>`, which commits only the named paths regardless of index state. PROTOCOL.md's rule about explicit staging is necessary but NOT sufficient under concurrency — it should require the pathspec form. Separately, one commit failed outright with 'cannot lock ref HEAD' when another auditor committed concurrently; retrying immediately succeeded.
